MGIMS Participates in ‘Swasth Nari, Sashakt Parivar Abhiyaan’ to Strengthen Women and Family Healthcare
Wednesday, 17 September 2025
1672 Hits
Sevagram, September 17, 2025
– Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram, participated in the “Swasth Nari, Sashakt Parivar Abhiyaan”, a nationwide health initiative aimed at improving healthcare access, quality of services, and awareness for women and their families.
“The two-week-long programme, running from September 17 to October 2, 2025, will feature health camps, awareness drives, maternal and child health services, and screening initiatives across Kasturba Hospital and its community outreach areas. Special focus will be laid on antenatal care, anaemia prevention, nutritional support, tuberculosis, family planning, and non-communicable disease screening among women,” informed Dr. Poonam Shivkumar Verma (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital).
The inaugural programme was presided over by Shri P. L. Tapadiyaji (President, Kasturba Health Society). Other dignitaries present included Dr. B. S. Garg (Secretary, KHS), Dr. A. K. Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr. Poonam Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital), Mrs. Sujata Taksande (Sarpanch, Sewagram), and Mrs. Sunita Dhawale (Sarpanch, Warud). The event was attended by senior faculty members, healthcare professionals, staff, and community representatives.
Speaking at the launch, Shri Tapadiya underlined the significance of KHS’s continued efforts in rural healthcare and community outreach, aligning with the Abhiyaan’s mission. He remarked,
“Gandhiji chose to name this hospital after Kasturba Gandhi when it was established in 1944. This reflects our deep and longstanding commitment towards women’s welfare, which continues to guide our work even today.”
Dr. Shuchi Jain (Head of Obstetrics & Gynecology, MGIMS), highlighted the need for holistic and inclusive healthcare for women and children, emphasizing that healthier women lead to empowered families and stronger communities. Dr. Bharti Taksande (Professor of Medicine, MGIMS), remarked,
“Lack of awareness, social stigma and limited access to healthcare often lead to undiagnosed diseases in women. Let us take a pledge to promote equal healthcare and support women.”
